answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through radio time-difference-of-arrival localization. Each agent broadcasts ultra-wideband pulses measured by a receiver grove to verify a unique physical position. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying discrete radio transceivers across separate coordinates. However, multipath reflections from obstacles like a coastal jetty or dense juniper shrubs introduce timing jitter, falsely invalidating legitimate agents.
